Article 13
(1) The community as referred to in Article 10 letter c has the obligation and responsibility for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
(2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include: a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Garut Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Garut. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency. 6. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 11. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 12. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 13. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 14. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the scope of the household. 15. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 16. Guardian is a person or entity who in reality exercises parental authority as a Parent over a Child. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 19. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Garut Regency area. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanisms of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of acts of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment, or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 27. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 30.

Article 11
(1) Regional Governments as referred to in Article 10 letter a, have the obligation and responsibility to:
a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement protection of women and children from violence;
c. supervise services for victims of violence based on minimum service standards in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; and
d. allocate budget for the protection of women and children from violence in accordance with regional financial capacity.
(2) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), Regional Governments formulate programs and activities for protective action for women and children in regional action plans which form part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.

Article 14
(1) Parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in Article 10 letter d legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence, report when violence occurs and protect victims.
(2) In the event that the parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) are absent or their whereabouts are unknown or, for a certain reason, cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members, to be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VII
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM VIOLENCE

Article 39
(1) Reporting on the implementation of the provision of protection for women and children from violence shall be carried out by:
a. P2TP2A to the Regent;
b. the Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-District Level to the Sub-District Head; and
c. the Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village/Urban Village Level to the Village Head/Urban Village Head.
(2) Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted in writing, covering:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
(3) Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causing the death of women and/or children.
(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering on women and/or children.
(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: 
 a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
  1) physical harassment;
  2) verbal harassment;
  3) gestural harassment;
  4) written or pictorial harassment; and
  5) psychological/emotional harassment.
 b. forced sexual intercourse;
 c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
 d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
 a. acts that result in a child's needs not being reasonably fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
 b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
 c. acts of deliberately neglecting a woman within the scope of the household, whereas according to the law applicable to the person concerned or due to consent or an agreement or contract, that person is obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such woman.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
 a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
 b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, subjugation, extortion, exploitation of the physical body, sexual exploitation, exploitation of reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues, or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
 c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution activities or sexual abuse.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 12
(1) The Village Government as referred to in Article 10 letter b, has the obligation and responsibility to:
a. prepare and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement the protection of women and children from violence;
c. supervise services for victims of violence based on minimum service standards in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; and
d. allocate budget for the protection of women and children from violence in accordance with the village's financial capacity.
(2) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Village Government prepares programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the Village action plan which is part of the Village Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMDes).

Article 3

CHAPTER XII
SANCTIONS
Article 41
(1) Every person who intentionally does not provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows the occurrence of violence, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of organizing protection, that does not carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
(3) The Management of P2TP2A, Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-District Level, Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village/Urban Village Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within the internal institution or respective organization.

Article 36
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector, NGOs/social organizations concerned with women and children in the protection of women and children against acts of violence.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are set forth in the form of agreements in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 26
(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 15 letter c constitutes services provided by assistants/companions to restore the traumatic condition of victims.

    b. psychological recovery of victims;
    c. accompanying victims and the victims’ parents in the family and community environment; and

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Garut Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Garut. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency. 6. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 11. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 12. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 13. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 14. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the scope of the household. 15. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 16. Guardian is a person or entity who in reality exercises parental authority as a Parent over a Child. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 19. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Garut Regency area. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanisms of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of acts of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment, or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 27. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 30.

Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causing the death of women and/or children.
(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering on women and/or children.
(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: 
 a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
  1) physical harassment;
  2) verbal harassment;
  3) gestural harassment;
  4) written or pictorial harassment; and
  5) psychological/emotional harassment.
 b. forced sexual intercourse;
 c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
 d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
 a. acts that result in a child's needs not being reasonably fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
 b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
 c. acts of deliberately neglecting a woman within the scope of the household, whereas according to the law applicable to the person concerned or due to consent or an agreement or contract, that person is obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such woman.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
 a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
 b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, subjugation, extortion, exploitation of the physical body, sexual exploitation, exploitation of reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues, or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
 c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution activities or sexual abuse.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 13
(1) The community as referred to in Article 10 letter c has the obligation and responsibility for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
(2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include: a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 3
The purpose of the regulation regarding the protection of women and children from acts of violence is to provide guidance and direction for the Regional Government and the community in carrying out prevention, services and social rehabilitation of women and children victims of acts of violence.

Article 11

4.4.rationale: Pasal 16 ayat (1) explicitly lists prevention methods including: (d) "melakukan sosialisasi" of relevant laws/regulations and (e) "memberikan pengetahuan tentang pencegahan dan mekanisme penanggulangan kekerasan" (providing knowledge about prevention and mechanisms to address violence). These are education/awareness-raising measures aimed at prevention. The English candidate passage accurately reflects this. Thus the judge’s 'Yes' aligns with the Indonesian text, suggesting the golden label 'No' is wrong (unless the indicator required a narrower school-based curriculum, which is not stated in the discrepancy description).

5.6.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly references mass media in the context of protecting victims’ privacy and confidentiality from coverage, indicating recognition of media as a relevant stakeholder to be managed within service provision.

(2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include: a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 36
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector, NGOs/social organizations concerned with women and children in the protection of women and children against acts of violence.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are set forth in the form of agreements in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 11
(1) Regional Governments as referred to in Article 10 letter a, have the obligation and responsibility to:
a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement protection of women and children from violence;
c. supervise services for victims of violence based on minimum service standards in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; and
d. allocate budget for the protection of women and children from violence in accordance with regional financial capacity.
(2) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), Regional Governments formulate programs and activities for protective action for women and children in regional action plans which form part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.

Article 41
(1) Every person who intentionally does not provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows the occurrence of violence, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of organizing protection, that does not carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.

5.6.rationale: The Indonesian text mentions media only in Pasal 21 huruf f: "menjaga privasi dan kerahasiaan korban ... termasuk pemberitaan oleh media massa" (protect privacy/confidentiality including mass media coverage). This is a confidentiality requirement, not a policy of engaging media as stakeholders (e.g., partnering with media for campaigns, guidelines for journalists, outreach/communication strategy). The judge treated mere mention of media in a restriction context as satisfying 'media engagement', which is an overly broad interpretation. Since the relevant passage was retrieved and correctly translated, the error is primarily the judge’s reasoning rather than retrieval/translation.
